display.title: Episode 516: The Mystery of Toras Emes (Purim Katan)
display.summary_short: On Purim Katan, Uncle Yossi teaches how to start the day with 'Shivisi Hashem' and Modeh Ani, then tells how a rabbi's dream foiled a plot to greet the king with an empty Sefer Torah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Purim Katan, the 14th of Adar Rishon in a leap year. Uncle Yossi explains Purim Katan and prays that by Purim we will celebrate a 'big Purim' with Moshiach. Returning to the Shulchan Aruch, he teaches that the first thought each morning is 'Shivisi Hashem', to picture Hashem before us, since Hashem guards us all night and never sleeps. We think those words but do not say them, because Hashem's name may not be said before washing our hands; then we say Modeh Ani, which has no Divine name. Starting the day this way fills us with joy. After the Hakochainik march, a young Tzivos Hashem member says the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: the Jews of a kind king's city greet him each year with a Sefer Torah. A jealous officer persuades the shul's shammes to use a beautiful but empty 'Torah' instead, then tells the king he is being mocked. Three times in a dream a voice tells the rabbi 'Toras Emes, a true Torah', and he quietly swaps in a real one. Like Haman, the plotter is punished. The show ends with candle-lighting times and Purim Katan wishes.
display.lesson: Hashem never sleeps and always guards the Jewish people; begin each day remembering He is before you, and serve Him with joy.

date.note: 'Tonight it's Purim Katan' in a leap year; Tuesday 14 Adar I 5752. Candle time 5:18.

advisories.note: A jealous officer plots to turn the king against the Jews; the king threatens severe punishment.

sources_cited.note: 'The Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.'
